content.title: About
content.content: Egg salad with mayonnaise (1957) is a classic cold dish made from hard‑boiled eggs, mayonnaise, and sometimes additions such as mustard, herbs, or onion. It is popular as a snack, side dish, and sandwich filling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first egg‑salad‑with‑mayonnaise recipe appeared in American cookbooks in the late 1950s.
The salad is often served in small portions at holiday tables, especially in the US and Canada.
Variations may include celery, dill, capers, or smoked salmon.
Mayonnaise can be swapped for yogurt or sour cream for a lighter version.
Egg salad is frequently used as a filling for sandwiches, wraps, and stuffed vegetables.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs provide a complete source of protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs supply B12, riboflavin, and folate, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Source of choline
items.content: Choline is important for liver health and cognitive processes.

items.title: Provides healthy fats
items.content: Mayonnaise made from vegetable oils adds monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and fat helps maintain a feeling of fullness longer.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg whites or yolks.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Mayonnaise makes the salad calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable for weight‑watching diets.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Improperly cooked or stored eggs can harbor Salmonella.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Egg yolks contain cholesterol; people with elevated cholesterol should consume in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the egg salad chilled as an appetizer, in sandwiches, on lettuce leaves, or as a stuffing for vegetables. Fresh herbs, mustard, or a squeeze of lemon can brighten the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
